procedure: IDENTICAL to R2: same paired design, same bootstrap (rng 7, n_boot 20000, alpha 0.05), same gate, one block, no extension, no new statistic

gates.rule: LCB95 > 0 in BOTH directions; no magnitude floor by design

the_mechanism.D_did_not_fall: discordant pairs ROSE, 94->99 on A and 82->88 on B
the_mechanism.reading: the specialists disagree slightly MORE often, but when they disagree the correct specialist now wins roughly three times in four instead of barely better than a coin flip. This is the 'similar number of disagreements, correct specialist dominates them' route, not the 'fewer disagreements' route.
the_mechanism.why_R2_failed: R2's failure was never directional -- both point estimates had the right sign. The disagreements were too BALANCED (55v39, 47v35), so Var(d) = D/n - delta^2 stayed large and the LCBs crossed zero.

coincidence_checked_not_assumed.observation: WR(pi_B, A) = 0.4844 in BOTH R2 and SAPPO, exactly 93/192
coincidence_checked_not_assumed.conclusion: coincidence on a discrete 192-seed grid, not duplicated data

what_this_licenses.claim: vanilla PPO produced weak, statistically unreliable specialization; strategy anchoring converted it into a CONFIRMED complementary repertoire on an untouched block, under the identical procedure, with no threshold moved and no extension used
what_this_licenses.unlocks: EXPERIMENT 2 (K=2 latent compression) -- two specialists now demonstrably worth compressing
what_this_licenses.does_NOT_claim: that a latent network can hold both modes. That is exactly what Experiment 2 tests, and it is the first time in this campaign that question has been well-posed.

provenance.both_resumed_from: the original R1 1M terminals, NOT the accidental vanilla 1.5M checkpoints
